attempts.prompt:
Korean webtoon panel, digitally inked and coloured by a professional webtoon studio. Crisp black ink with tapered strokes, heavier on the outer silhouette, the jaw, the hair mass and where forms overlap. Flat local colour with one hard-edged cool cel shadow per material. One named key light: its colour washes smoothly over the lit side. If the scene names a back light, it draws a thin crisp rim along the figure's silhouette. Everything else stays flat. Muted cool base palette of slate, navy and grey-blue, so the light source and the character's signature colour carry the saturation. Background simplified and lower in contrast than the characters. Small crisp highlights; glossy specular only on metal and wet surfaces.
Hand-made webtoon colouring: each garment has only a few large, opaque, clean-edged shadow shapes, placed in its real folds; no scattered translucent streaks, zigzag shards or crumpled-foil folds. Worn cloth shows a few small frayed notches and loose threads, never sawtooth edges along every edge. Plain shoes and clothes with no logos, stripes or brand marks. Every strap, buckle, pocket and seam is attached and has a purpose; no stray stitch marks. Matte skin, hair and stone; no 3D, low-poly or plastic look.
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: S23 Arc 4 crew FRONT model lineup, the unmasked identity master, filename lineup_faces.png. Native canvas 1536 by 1024 pixels, landscape PNG. Flat light-grey #E9E9EC edge to edge, no texture or vignette. Soft neutral upper-left key light. Straight-on full-body model-sheet camera about 1.25 m high with negligible perspective; five figures on one baseline, same physical scale. Feet near the bottom, tall figures filling almost the full image height, heads uncut. A lineup is specifically required here. Only the five crew members below, left to right. No silhouette, scale man, ruler, height ticks, labels or inset portraits.
Reference image 1 is APPROVED Kang Jaeha front: use it ONLY for the fourth person's existing face, messy hair, skin, fingerless gloves, plain boots and hand-inked V2 finish. Replace his entire hoodie and vest costume with the crew kit below. Do not copy the T, reflective strips, safety vest pockets or pose.
All five wear grey work coveralls #747B83 with cool shadow #505A66, a simple waist-length to upper-thigh orange tabard #F26A1B over them, and practical black work boots. The tabard is a plain sleeveless front-and-back rectangular cloth bib tied at the sides, with a large EMPTY smooth orange area centered on chest and back for the letterer to add numbers later; absolutely NO drawn number or letter on any tabard. The full-face respirators are pushed down around their necks, resting on the upper chest: a smoky tinted visor and TWO round filters, secured by visible connected straps. Their faces are completely unobscured above the masks. HARD HATS ARE REMOVED and kept outside this image, not held or floating. No helmets anywhere in this unmasked sheet. Coveralls remain properly fitted, not baggy inflated bodies; adults about 7.5 heads high, legs about half their height.
Left to right exactly:
1. Pyo Dongsik, 63, 160 cm, small wiry elderly Korean man, short grey crew cut, weathered kindly lined face, small smile with visibly crooked teeth. A functional black brace around his anatomical LEFT knee (viewer-right knee of this figure), connected padded support and straps. Slightly favoring that bad knee, both hands loosely holding the top sides of his tabard. Clearly old, not frail or a caricature.
2. Dami, 34, 164 cm (design choice where height is unspecified), tired Korean single mother with dark under-eye marks, oval face, dark-brown eyes, black hair in a low bun visible behind the neck, no glamour makeup. One hand holds a plain dark phone down at her waist with its BACK facing viewer, screen hidden; the other touches her respirator strap. Her posture reads exhausted but steady.
3. Jang Woo, 25, 184 cm (height design choice), lanky Korean man with conspicuously large ears, short black hair, long narrow face, slim neck, easy older-brother half-smile. Hands lightly holding opposite sides of his tabard. Not bulky.
4. Kang Jaeha, 24, 178 cm, the referenced lean young Korean man, narrow oval face and angular cheekbones, straight nose, heavy upper eyelids and tired lines, dark brown eyes. Messy near-black hair with a long fringe over anatomical LEFT eye (picture-right side of HIS face); yellow pencil behind anatomical RIGHT ear (picture-left of HIS face). Same black fingerless gloves and black work boots as approved front; grey crew COVERALLS and orange blank TABARD instead of hoodie and vest; notebook hidden INSIDE the tabard, not visible outside. Polite slight close-mouth smile. One hand at tabard's side tie, other on respirator rim.
5. Jang Ho, 23, 181 cm (height design choice), lanky Korean man with the SAME prominent big ears and family facial structure as Woo, younger rounder cheeks and short BLEACHED pale blond hair with dark roots. A tentative grin. Holding his own tabard edges.
Keep Pyo shortest, Dami next, then Jaeha, Ho, Woo tallest. Same scale and common baseline, not equal height. Each person separated by a narrow clear gap, no overlaps hiding knee brace or silhouettes, wrists attached and five fingers per hand. Restraint in folds: a few broad opaque shadows, clean hand-drawn lines, no fine fabric grain, no shards or optical softness.
No text, letters, numbers, speech bubbles, captions, sound-effect lettering, interface windows or readable signs. Emblems without letters are fine; no brand logos or wordmarks. Not a 3D render, not a photograph, no photographic background. No airbrushed skin, no plastic gloss on skin or hair, no haze or bloom over the whole image, no depth-of-field blur, no lens flare unless a real camera flash is in the scene. No watermark or signature. Correct hands with five fingers. No chibi proportions unless the brief says chibi. No compressed or stubby bodies, no shortened legs or torsos, no oversized heads; no people out of scale with the doors, vehicles and buildings around them; no figures floating off the floor or breaking the scene's perspective.
attempts.reason: Jaeha retains dark navy trousers rather than the grey crew coveralls; clothing shadows too fragmented.
